title: Pointwise smoothness of an lfp scheme morphism under flat base change
statement: Let $f:U\to V$ be a locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $g:T\to V$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Put $U_T=U\times_VT$, with projections $p:U_T\to U$ and $f_T:U_T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $u_T\in |U_T|$, the morphism $f_T$ is smooth at $u_T$ if and only if $f$ is smooth at $p(u_T)$. Smooth at a point means smooth on some open neighbourhood, with smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Neither flatness of $f$ nor local finite presentation or surjectivity of $g$ is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $z\in U_T$, and put $u=p(z)$, $t=f_T(z)$ and $v=g(t)=f(u)$. First suppose $f$ is smooth at $u$, and choose an open neighbourhood $N\subset U$ on which $f$ is smooth. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $N\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] to this morphism and the arbitrary map $g$: its base change is smooth at the point over $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], that base change is the open neighbourhood $p^{-1}(N)$ of $z$ in $U_T$, with its morphism to $T$ the restriction of $f_T$. This proves ascent.

source.place: Tag 02V4, lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth, the forward inclusion; case (1) applied on a smooth neighbourhood; Tag 01VF, lemma-smooth-flat

proof.text: For reflection assume $f_T$ is smooth at $z$. Its restriction to some open neighbourhood of $z$ is smooth, hence flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Stalks of an open subscheme at its points are the original stalks, so this says that $f_T$ is flat at $z$ in [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The hypothesis that $g$ is flat gives flatness at $t$ by that same definition. Clause (2) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change] therefore gives flatness of $f$ at $u$. We have not asserted that $f$ is flat at other points. Also $f_T$ is locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 02V4, case (2), reflection of flatness; Tag 047C, more-morphisms-lemma-flat-locus-base-change, clause (2), for the structure sheaf; Tag 01TS

proof.text: Let $w_T\in (U_T)_t$ and $w\in U_v$ be the unique fibre points above $z$ and $u$, respectively; these exist by the homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] to $f_T$ at $z$, using its local finite presentation and pointwise flatness from step 2. It follows that $(U_T)_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is smooth at $w_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change], this fibre is the base change of $U_v\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ along the induced residue-field map. The comparison sends $w_T$ to $w$: its compatibility with the projections to $U$ sends it to $p(z)=u$, and the fibre projection is injective on points.

source.place: Tag 02V4, displayed identity for fibres of a base change; Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, (1) iff (2)

proof.text: The fibre map $U_v\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], since its base is a field. It is locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] to this flat locally finitely presented fibre morphism and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$. By the comparison and point identification of step 3, smoothness at $w_T$ implies smoothness of $U_v\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ at $w$. This invokes case (1) only on the fibre, whose flatness is known independently.

source.place: Tag 02V4, fibrewise comparison in the first paragraph, using its already established case (1) over the residue field instead of repeating Algebra Tag 02UQ

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] to $f$ at $u$: local finite presentation is an original hypothesis, flatness at $u$ is step 2, and smoothness of its fibre at $w$ is step 4. Thus $f$ is smooth at $u$. Together with step 1 this gives the asserted equivalence for every $z$. If $U_T$ is empty there is no point to check; none of these arguments requires surjectivity or finite presentation of $g$.
